Ashok S. Kinagi, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of M.V Act, being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chincholi, dated 16.09.2022 in MVC No.405/2020, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short) seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

NC: 2024:KHC-K:4922-DB Appellant is the petitioner and the respondents are the respondents.
3. Brief facts leading rise to filing of the appeal are as under:
On 06.10.2019, the petitioner was proceeding from his house towards agricultural land in his motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-32-ED-9578 at about 12.15 p.m,
when he was near Sangyo cross within the limits of Bhakthampalli village, at that time, a Force Trax Toofan vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-37-M-2694 being driven by its driver came from opposite direction with high speed in rash and negligent manner and hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down from his motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner was self employed and earning Rs.4 lakhs p.a.

Due to accidental injuries,
the petitioner is unable to attend his work as he is suffering from permanent Nagireddy @ Nagareddy vs Lalusha And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145306643/
2 disability.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act seeking compensation of NC: 2024:KHC-K:4922-DB Rs.25,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained in the road traffic accident and accordingly prays to allow the claim petition.
4. Respondent No.1 filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.

It is stated that the said vehicle was insured and driver of the offending vehicle was possessing a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and the liability is on the insurance company to pay the claim amount.

Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition against respondent No.1.
5.
Respondent No.2 filed the written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

It is contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid driving license as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition.
The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings of the parties, framed the issues for its consideration.
7. In order to substantiate the case, petitioner herein got examined himself as PW.1.
In order to prove the disability, examined the doctor as PW.2 and got marked 13 documents as Exs.P1 to P13.
The respondents neither led oral nor documentary evidence.

8. The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence allowed the claim petition in part with costs and it is held that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,36,838/- along with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of realization and respondent No.2 was liable to pay the compensation amount and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of 60 days from the date of award.
9. Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed this NC: 2024:KHC-K:4922-DB miscellaneous first appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.
10. We have heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company.

11. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner in order to prove his permanent disability examined a doctor as PW.2, who has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability of 60% to the whole body, wherein the tribunal considered 1/3rd of the total disability assessed by PW.2.
He submits that PW.2 is the doctor, who is expert in the medical field.
The Tribunal ought to have taken atleast  of the disability assessed by PW.2.
He submits that the Tribunal has awarded lesser compensation under all heads.

Hence, on these grounds, he prays to Nagireddy @ Nagareddy vs Lalusha And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145306643/
3 allow the appeal.

sentences.text: 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company supports the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, contending NC: 2024:KHC-K:4922-DB that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is just and proper and same does not call for any interference by this court.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.
13. We have perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The point that arises for our consideration is with regard to quantum.

14. It is not in dispute that the petitioner met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
laceration on the right hand, abrasion on right thigh, abrasion on right tibia and other injuries which caused permanent disablement.

Further, in order to establish that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner produced certified copy of FIR marked as Ex.P1 and produced certified copy of the charge sheet marked as Ex.P3.
From the perusal of Ex.P3, it discloses that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Insofar as Disability is concerned:
15. The petitioner examined a doctor as PW.2, who has issued disability certificate.

As per Ex.P9 which discloses that PW.2 on clinical examination of PW.1 has issued a disability certificate marked as Ex.P9, which discloses that PW.2 has examined PW.1 on 10.11.2021 and he has also verified the wound certificate and discharge card.

He has opined that PW.1 had fracture of both bones of right leg which was treated by CRIF with interlocking rod on 06.10.2019 and skin grafting on 17.10.2019 and there was also fracture of right tibia.
The following permanent disability as per the guidelines given by the Ministry of Social Justice Empowerment, GOI, June 2001 and combined formula a+b (90-a) /90 .
Thus, PW.2 has assessed the disability suffered by PW.1 i.e., 60% to the whole body and also opined that the patient needs one more surgery for removal of implant which costs Rs.1,00,000/-.
We have perused the evidence of PW.2 and also wound certificate, discharge summary card.

The petitioner was admitted in the hospital for 17 days from NC:
2024:KHC-K:4922-DB 06.10.2019 and discharged on 23.10.2019.
He has undergone a surgery and a rod was implanted.
From the over all evidence of PW.2 and discharge summary card, we are of the opinion that permanent disability assessed by the Tribunal is on lower side, which needs to be enhanced.
Thus, we enhance the permanent disability at 25% considering over all evidence of petitioner and witness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.13,250 X 12X 14 X25% =
Rs.5,56,500/- under the head of 'loss of future income'.
16. Thus, we have re-assessed the compensation under the following different heads:

 Towards food and extra  nourishment and medical 6,800/- 20,000/-
 attendant  Towards conveyance 5,000/- 20,000/-
 Towards loss of income  during laid up period 26,500/- 39,750/-
 (13,250 X3)
 - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:4922-DB  Towards loss of future 3,33,900/- 5,56,500/-
 income  Deprivation of future 5,000/- 30,000/-
 amenities  Total Rs.5,36,838/- Rs.8,60,888/-
 Enhanced by this Court Rs. 3,24,050/-
 17.
The petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.8,60,888/- as against Rs.5,36,838/- awarded by the tribunal.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.3,24,050/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
18.

Hence, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
(c) The petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.8,60,888/- as against Rs.5,36,838/- awarded by the tribunal.
The petitioner is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.3,24,050/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
